newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB Report-Weather takes role as leading factor.
newsitem.headline: AWB Report-Weather takes role as leading factor.

text.p: The Australian wheat market was driven by weather factors this week after being led last week by demand, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said in its weekly grain market report on Friday.
Rainfall in Victoria state and drying off of cattle over the last few weeks contributed to a drop in demand, the AWB said.
Total shipments of 81,152 tonnes this week was down sharply from the 185,152 tonnes shipped last week, the AWB said.
Most wheat during the week was shipped to Spain, Iraq and South Korea, it said.
A reduction in the AWB's pool tender reserve offer and higher grower sales contributed to a rise in supply and dampening of the market, the AWB said.
"The tender price is now comparative to cash market prices at around US$10 lower than previously," the AWB said.
New crop sowing is progressing well as a result of the recent rain, the board said. However, it said the West Mallee and other southern pockets still require moisture.
